## What this project is

Astro Research is an open laboratory for comparing classical Vedic astrological
principles with what actually happened: earthquakes, floods, market prices and
national events. Every principle, dataset, script and result is public, and the
project is built so that astrologers can add the principles they want tested
without writing code.

The aim is to compare and contrast. A principle from a classical text is
stated precisely, matched against recorded dates and data, and the comparison
is published with the code that produced it, so that anyone can rerun it,
question it or extend it.

## How to read a comparison here

- **A rule** is one classical principle written down precisely: which planets,
  which configuration, which window of time, which kind of event it is said to
  relate to, and the text and verse it comes from.
- **A study** applies a set of rules to one kind of recorded event (for
  example, M5+ earthquakes since 2020, or the daily gold price) and compares
  the periods when a rule holds with the periods when it does not.
- **A result** is the outcome of that comparison: an effect size with its
  uncertainty, the test used, and how many rules were tested at the same time.
  Results are reported as found, whether positive, null or mixed, and every
  figure links back to the script and data that made it.

The methods are described on the [Methods](methods.qmd) page.

## The principles in use

Each study draws on principles from classical texts such as the Brihat Parashara
Hora Shastra, Brihat Samhita, Phaladeepika and Saravali, for example
Mars-Ketu conjunctions in mundane astrology or the planetary lords of the
nakshatras. The [Principles](principles.qmd) page will list every rule in use
with its classical source and the studies that use it.

Astrologers are invited to propose more. A rule can be proposed without
writing code; see [Contribute](contribute.qmd).

## Studies and their status

The strip below is read from each study's `results.json` when the site is
built; it states what each study ran and counted, not a verdict. Each card
links to the study's paper, and the [explorers](explore/index.qmd) let you
filter and compare the same results.

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
{{< include components/provenance.ojs >}}
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
siteResults = FileAttachment("data/results.json").json()
htl.html`<div class="af-status" id="study-status">${siteResults.status.map((s) => htl.html`
  <div class="af-status-item">
    <h4><a href=${s.link}>${s.study}</a></h4>
    <span class="af-status-state">${s.status}</span>
    <p>${s.headline}</p>
  </div>`)}</div>`
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
rulesStrip = FileAttachment("data/rules.json").json()
htl.html`<div class="af-status" id="rule-status">${[
  ["confirmed", "Rules confirmed", "passed their one confirmation run on held-out data"],
  ["tuned", "Rules tuned", "tuned on an exploration period; confirmation pending"],
  ["unvalidated", "Rules unvalidated", "stated and coded, not yet tested on a holdout"]
].map(([k, title, text]) => htl.html`<div class="af-status-item">
    <h4><a href=${`principles.html`}>${rulesStrip.validation_counts[k]} ${title.toLowerCase().replace("rules ", "")}</a></h4>
    <span class="af-status-state">${title}</span><p>${text}${k === "confirmed" && rulesStrip.validation_counts.not_confirmed
      ? `; ${rulesStrip.validation_counts.not_confirmed} more were tested and not confirmed` : ""}.</p></div>`)}</div>`
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
provenance(siteResults._meta, { twin: null, note: "one card per study, from its artifacts/results.json" })
```

Earlier results were withdrawn on 2026-11-08 because some figures were
generated from simulated data and planetary positions were tropical rather than
sidereal. The [Corrections](corrections.qmd) page records what was withdrawn and
why; corrected results will be published here as they are computed.
